text:
carla: Quick RFC follow-up. I'm proposing we bifurcate the console UI query path into two specialized flows: an 'edge-projection' path for panel rendering (fast, cached, predicate-pushed) and an 'interactive-query' path for ad-hoc/longer queries. Aim: reduce tail latency for dashboards, simplify caching, and keep a clear RBAC boundary.

david: Can you sketch the two flows at a high level?

carla: Sure — rough sketch: edge receives request -> authN/authZ at edge -> route to projection service (returns pre-projected rows/aggregates) -> render panel. If panel requests complex joins or full rows, forward to interactive-query pool. Important: projection service must get predicate pushdown and policy context so results are correct.

carla: Example config idea:```yaml
panels:
  - id: recent-queries
    type: projection
    columns: [id, user_display, result_summary]
    cache_ttl: 30s
    policy_key: org_policy_hash
```

alice: Pushing RBAC to edge worries me for row-level filters — how do we guarantee correctness? Edge is trusted but we can’t push everything to the projection layer without leaking.

carla: Agreement: we don't *only* trust edge. Plan: compile policies centrally into a canonical predicate AST + hash. Edge supplies the policy_hash with the request. Projection service validates the predicate against the canonical compiler output. For joins/derived data we fallback to interactive-query which enforces final policy checks. Cache keys include policy_hash so stale policies don’t serve wrong data.

ben: Policy-hash-in-cache key will cause invalidation storms when policies change. How often do policy changes happen? For org-wide rules maybe rare, but user-level filters (scoped roles) could be frequent.

carla: Good point. Mitigation: multi-tier cache keys — long-lived caches for org/static policies, short TTL per-user caches for user-scoped filters. Also emit invalidation events on policy update via pubsub to nuke relevant projection caches. We should measure invalidation rate in canary.

sophie: What's the cost overhead? Duplicate projection service plus metadata + cache store seems like extra infra.

carla: Tradeoffs: projection storage is mostly column-subset and pre-aggregates (expect ~1.1–1.3x storage for projection materialized shapes). But CPU cost could be lower because we avoid full join evaluation for the common dashboard panels; we expect p99 latency drop and lower DB query cost at scale. Need to validate with a staging traffic replay.

david: Let's run a canary: baseline vs bifurcated path, 2 weeks, ~10k dashboard hits/day. Track p50/p95/p99, cache hit rate, invalidation events, and infra spend delta.

carla: I'll PR the RFC with sequence diagrams, failure modes (cache staleness, policy mismatch, projection regen race), and rollout plan: 1) enable projection path behind flag for 10% of traffic, 2) observe metrics, 3) increase and run chaos tests.

carla: TL;DR: edge RBAC + projection cache removes a lot of DB join pressure for dashboards and should cut tail latency, but adds policy-hash complexity + invalidation semantics. Need experiments to validate economics.

deploy-bot: canary created: console-query-bifurcation/v1 -> staging (10% traffic). :rocket:

alice: Thanks — will skim RFC and add comments on the exact policy AST we emit.

ben: I'll hook up cost dashboard for the canary.

carla: Thanks all. Follow-up PR link will be in #eng-runtime when ready.
